page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.small is a single-core virtual machine instance configured with 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 8.0 GB of memory. It runs on a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor based on the x86_64 architecture, supported by the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (Foundation and VNNI), AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance type includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent filesystems, and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark results place the processing and memory subsystems predominantly in the lower percentiles relative to modern cloud infrastructure. The instance scored 1015.38 on stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations, and registered a Geekbench single-core score of 939 alongside a multi-core score of 937. Memory throughput reaches 80.64 GB/sec for small cached blocks but drops to 8.76 GB/sec for large un-cached reads and 7.12 GB/sec for writes. Application benchmarks show 1.31 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 1.27 GB/sec throughput for static web delivery.

With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the ecs.e3.small provides higher memory density per compute thread than standard configurations. However, execution speed is strictly bounded by single-core compute performance and limited memory bandwidth. The instance is suited for lightweight memory-resident utilities, small staging databases, background queue workers, and basic web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over high throughput.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.small is a virtual instance featuring 1 dedicated vCPU on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. Built on x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor, it includes instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and AES. The instance provides no bundled local storage and operates without hardware GPU acceleration. Performance metrics place its compute throughput in the bottom tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 939, a PassMark CPU score of 1307.43, and large-block memory read speeds of 8.76 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 1.31 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.27 GB/sec in static web throughput. Given its 8 GB per vCPU memory ratio and modest single-threaded capacity, the instance fits low-volume memory-centric tasks, development environments, and small background caching tiers.
